आषाढी वारी - श्रद्धा, भक्ती, परंपरा आणि महाराष्ट्राच्या संस्कृतीचा दिव्य सोहळा! मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली विधान भवन, मुंबई येथे तीर्थक्षेत्र पंढरपूर येथील आषाढी एकादशीच्या पूर्वतयारीसंदर्भात आढावा बैठक पार पडली. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले की, आषाढी वारी ही वारकरी संप्रदायाच्या श्रद्धेचा आणि महाराष्ट्राच्या सांस्कृतिक परंपरेचा महत्त्वपूर्ण सोहळा आहे. यंदाच्या वारीत लाखो भाविकांची कोणतीही गैरसोय होणार नाही यासाठी सर्व विभागांच्या समन्वयातून व्यापक नियोजन करण्यात यावे. तसेच वारीचा उपक्रम डिस्कव्हरी आणि नॅशनल जिओग्राफिक दूरचित्रवाहिन्यांद्वारे जगभरात पोहोचणार असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी स्पष्ट केले. मागील वर्षी 'निर्मल वारी' उपक्रम प्रभावीपणे राबविण्यात आला असून यंदाचीही वारी सर्वांच्या सहकार्याने आणि पांडुरंगाच्या आशीर्वादाने यशस्वीपणे पार पडेल असे नियोजन करावे, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी दिले. यंदाच्या वारीसाठी पालखी मार्गावरील रस्त्यांची मोठ्या प्रमाणात दुरुस्ती व मजबुतीकरणाची कामे करण्यात आली आहेत. तसेच राष्ट्रीय महामार्ग प्राधिकरणाच्या माध्यमातून विविध विकासकामे पूर्ण करण्यात आली आहेत. त्यामुळे पालखी मार्गावरील प्रवास अधिक सुरक्षित आणि सुलभ होणार आहे. वारकऱ्यांच्या मुक्कामस्थळी मोठ्या प्रमाणावर जर्मन हँगर उभारण्यात आले असून संतश्रेष्ठ श्री ज्ञानेश्वर महाराज, जगदगुरु संत श्री तुकाराम महाराज तसेच इतर पालख्यांच्या मुक्कामस्थळी जर्मन हँगरची व्यवस्था करण्यात आली आहे. यामुळे लाखो वारकऱ्यांना सुरक्षित आणि प्रशस्त निवासाची सुविधा उपलब्ध होणार आहे, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी सांगितले. पुणे विभागाबाहेरील पालख्यांनाही सर्व सोयी सुविधा उपलब्ध करून देण्यात येतील. त्यासाठी सोलापूर जिल्ह्याचे पालकमंत्री यांची नोडल पालकमंत्री व पुणे विभागीय आयुक्त यांची नोडल अधिकारी म्हणून नियुक्ती करण्यात येत आहे. डीजे मुक्त वारी सोहळ्यासाठी पोलीस प्रशासनाने सर्वांशी चर्चा करून प्रयत्न करावेत. वारी सोहळा हा पारंपरिक पद्धतीनेच साजरा करण्याचे आवाहनही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी केले. पालखी सोहळा प्रमुखांनी केलेल्या मागण्यांचा सकारात्मक विचार केला जाईल असेही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी सांगितले. The first known appearance of the US-made Mobile Anti-Air Weapons Launcher – Reconfigurable (MAAWLR) short-range air defense system in Ukraine. In the footage, the vehicle, developed by the American Sierra Nevada Corporation company, can be seen being targeted by a Russian FPV drone. MAAWLR is a light, low-cost platform dedicated for countering unmanned aerial vehicles. The system is based on the Battery Revolving Adaptive Weapons Launcher - Reconfigurable (BRAWLR) established on a pick-up chassis. The BRAWLR can have its pylons swapped to fire a wide variety of munitions, including AIM-9, AIM-120, AIM-132, IRIS-T, APKWS II and R-27. The vehicle is also equipped with the MX-15 optoelectronic complex for target detection and tracking. It isn't publicly known how many MAAWLR air defense systems have been delivered to Ukraine.

मुज़फ्फरनगर में मजदूरों की बंधुआ मजदूरी का मामला बेहद चौंकाने वाला है। बिना मज़दूरी दिए काम करवाने के अलावा, मजदूरों को कुत्तों से कटवाया गया, भाले से गोदा गया, कोड़े मारे गए, और उन्हें मवेशियों का चारा खिलाया गया। यह इंसानी गरिमा पर हमला है - पीड़ितों को न्याय के साथ पुनर्वास और दोषियों को कड़ी से कड़ी सजा मिलनी चाहिए। साथ ही हमें यह भी पूछना ज़रूरी है कि मज़दूर ऐसी खतरनाक परिस्थितियों में किन मजबूरियों में फंस जाते हैं। जब रोज़गार ख़त्म हो जाते हैं, आमदनी ठहर जाती है, और सबसे कमज़ोर वर्गों के लिए बने मनरेगा और श्रम कानूनों जैसी सुरक्षाएं कमज़ोर कर दी जाती हैं, तो हताशा बढ़ती जाती है। जिन लोगों के पास कोई और विकल्प या सुरक्षा नहीं होती, वो ऐसे शोषण का आसान शिकार बन जाते हैं। यह कोई आम आपराधिक घटना नहीं है - यह एक धराशाई हुई अर्थव्यवस्था का मलबा है।

Polski Kontyngent Wojskowy w Turcji realizuje kluczowe misje we wschodniej części Morza Śródziemnego oraz nad Morzem Czarnym. Do głównych zadań kontyngentu należy prowadzenie działań patrolowo–rozpoznawczych, a także bieżące przekazywanie pozyskanych danych rozpoznawczych do struktur Sojuszu Północnoatlantyckiego (NATO), co wydatnie wzmacnia wspólną obronność i świadomość sytuacyjną sprzymierzeńców. Misja ta ewoluuje wraz z modernizacją Sił Zbrojnych RP. Zadania patrolowo–rozpoznawcze z bazy Incirlik realizowane są przez nowoczesne bezzałogowe statki powietrzne Bayraktar TB2, będące na wyposażeniu Wojska Polskiego. Wykorzystanie systemów bezzałogowych potwierdza wysokie kompetencje operacyjne polskich żołnierzy oraz zdolność do adaptacji najnowszych technologii na polu walki w strukturach międzynarodowych. Podczas wizyty w bazie wojskowej, wraz PKW Turcja Prezydent Nawrocki oglądał pokaz Bayraktarów wraz z żołnierzami.

Prezydent RP @NawrockiKn odwiedził bazę lotniczą İncirlik, pełniącą ważną rolę w strukturach Sojuszu Północnoatlantyckiego. To okazją do spotkania z żołnierzami z Polskiego Kontyngentu Wojskowego Turcja.

"Finally, countries across Europe and the northern hemisphere are experiencing an extreme heat wave. Extreme heat is one of the most serious and rapidly growing threats to health and safety posed by climate change. It claims around half a million lives globally each year, yet many of these deaths are preventable. Heat affects everyone, but those at highest risk include older adults, people with chronic conditions, children, pregnant women, workers exposed to extreme heat, and socially disadvantaged populations. Heatwaves can also become a major health hazard for people attending mass gatherings and sporting events. During the #FIFAWorldCup, WHO is collaborating with @FIFAcom and host countries on a “#BeatTheHeat initiative”, to develop action plans, raise awareness, establish early warning systems, improve access to safe drinking water, and implement cooling strategies and smart planning. Fans, workers, and event organisers are all exposed to heat. Protecting them sends a powerful signal: health must be at the centre of global events"-@DrTedros

"Now to the ongoing conflict in #Sudan. In the city of El Obeid in North Kordofan, the humanitarian situation continues to worsen. WHO echoes concerns raised by the UN Security Council over the imminent risk of mass atrocities, and supports the demand for an immediate halt to assaults. In neighbouring West Kordofan, the State Ministry of Health has reported 734 suspected cholera cases and 105 deaths, since the 15th of May. The outbreak is occurring in the context of health systems disrupted by long-running conflict. WHO and partners are responding to the outbreak by strengthening access to safe water and sanitation, establishing cholera treatment centres, prepositioning rapid diagnostic tests and medicines, and dispatching samples to South Sudan for testing"-@DrTedros

"Now to the outbreak of #hantavirus. The total number of cases from the hantavirus outbreak remains 13, including three deaths. In all, more than 650 contacts have been identified and followed up by local health authorities in 33 countries and territories. All but 54 contacts have completed their period of quarantine., and the remaining contacts are scheduled to complete their quarantine period by the 2nd of July. If no further cases are reported by then, WHO will consider the outbreak to be over. However, WHO will continue working to advance our understanding of this outbreak, and hantavirus more generally. Working with governments and partners, we are continuing investigations into how the outbreak started and spread among those on board. We are also working with partners who have collected environmental samples onboard the ship. In addition, we are coordinating a study among people exposed to the virus involving 21 countries, to better understand how the disease develops. We are also working on having a sample of the virus shared with the WHO BioHub in Switzerland. This will be important for developing diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines for future outbreaks. I thank all countries that have contributed in different ways to the response to this outbreak, with special thanks to the leadership and solidarity shown by Spain. I also thank the Captain of the MV Hondius, Captain Jan Dobrogowski, his crew and all passengers for their cooperation in what has been a very difficult situation"-@DrTedros

Russian security officials are trying to convince Russian President Vladimir Putin of the need to move up the parliamentary elections to the State Duma, which are scheduled for September 2026. These discussions have become more frequent as Ukrainian drones strike targets in Moscow, two sources close to Putin’s administration told Russian media outlet Meduza. According to the sources, the idea of postponing the elections is being pushed by the top leadership of the Russian FSB and the head of the Rosgvardia, Viktor Zolotov, a former bodyguard and friend of Putin’s. Meduza was told that postponing the elections could in fact mean “canceling them in the near future,” and discussions on this began as early as the spring of 2026. The source cites the country’s budget problems, rising prices, funding cuts, and layoffs at enterprises as reasons for postponing the elections—all of which are affecting the approval ratings of the ruling United Russia party, which currently stand at 35%.

Made in AL, tested in TX! Dave Limp (@davill) I've come to appreciate boring hotfires. Our BE-7 team recently completed a 2,500 second hotfire test at 10klbf on a development engine, setting the record for the longest-duration turbo pump-fed liquid rocket engine hotfire. ISLAMABAD: 24 June 2026. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif received a telephone call from His Royal Highness Prince Fahd Bin Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Governor of Tabuk Province, this afternoon. During their most warm and cordial conversation, His Royal Highness the Governor congratulated the Prime Minister on Pakistan’s remarkable diplomatic efforts that resulted in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the U.S. and Iran. The Prime Minister thanked His Royal Highness the Governor for his kind words and said that Pakistan’s peace efforts were aimed at ensuring regional peace and stability, with the support of brotherly countries, including Saudi Arabia. While recalling the historic brotherly ties between Pakistan and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Prime Minister expressed his deepest gratitude to His Royal Highness Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for his affection for Pakistan. The Prime Minister extended an invitation to His Royal Highness the Governor to undertake a visit to Pakistan.

Had a warm and most cordial telephone conversation with my dear brother, His Highness Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Amir of the State of Qatar, this afternoon. I thanked His Highness for Qatar’s steadfast support for the peace efforts that culminated in the historic Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. We expressed satisfaction at the positive progress made during the first round of technical talks in Bürgenstock and agreed on the importance of sustaining this momentum through continued dialogue and diplomacy. I also thanked His Highness for his kind condolences on the tragic loss of a Pakistani national in the recent fire incident in Ras Laffan, and expressed my deep appreciation to the Qatari leadership for its generous hospitality towards the vibrant Pakistani community in Qatar. Pakistan values its close brotherly ties with Qatar and looks forward to welcoming His Highness to Pakistan later this year.

These two instances, IIOJK and Palestine along with many others, across various parts of the world – whether covered by Security Council resolutions dealing with thematic issues, Ch. VI, Ch. VII sanctions, peacekeeping, conflict prevention, or country-specific situations demonstrate that implementation of Security Council resolutions must be treated as a central pillar of conflict prevention. In recent years as well, the Council has adopted resolutions that addressed specific situations, but could not ensure their implementation – thus piling up on top of those that remain unimplemented for decades. My statement at the Arria-Formula Meeting on “Bridging the Implementation Gap: Security Council Resolutions and the Maintenance of International Peace and Security” co-hosted by the Pakistan and China Missions to the UN

The same lesson is visible in case of Palestine. For decades, Security Council and General Assembly resolutions have affirmed the rights of the Palestinian people, the inadmissibility of acquisition of territory by force, the illegality of settlement activity, the need to end occupation, and the vision of Palestinian self-determination and statehood. Yet the persistent non-implementation of these resolutions has produced a catastrophic reality. Occupation has deepened. Settlements have expanded. Civilians, especially women and children, continue to bear unbearable suffering. My statement at the Arria-Formula Meeting on “Bridging the Implementation Gap: Security Council Resolutions and the Maintenance of International Peace and Security” co-hosted by the Pakistan and China Missions to the UN

The tragedy of Jammu and Kashmir is a pertinent example. For almost eight decades, the Kashmiri people have waited for the implementation of more than a dozen Security Council resolutions recognizing their right to determine their own future through a free and impartial plebiscite under UN auspices – that is self-determination. Let there be no ambiguity. These resolutions are solemn commitments of the international community and binding obligations under the Charter, yet remain unfulfilled due to non-implementation. And this non-implementation means: a major international dispute that remains unresolved, with consequences for international peace and security, and prolonged human suffering of the Kashmiri people. The Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) hosted a seminar titled “𝐓𝐚𝐱 𝐏𝐨𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐓𝐚𝐱𝐞𝐬,” featuring Dr. Cristian Lucas, Senior Economist at the World Bank, as the keynote speaker. The session was moderated by Dr. Nadia Hassan (@Nadiia_Hassan), Assistant Professor at PIDE. The seminar explored the evolving challenges of taxation in the digital economy, including the taxation of digital platforms, cross-border services, and emerging technologies. DMRC Commences Work at Central Secretariat Station for Central Vista Corridor The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has commenced construction work at the Central Secretariat Metro Station for the Central Vista Corridor today. The station is being developed under Phase V(A) as an extension of the existing Magenta Line from Janakpuri West to RK Ashram Marg. The event was graced by the august presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs and Power. In addition, Shri Katikithala Srinivas, Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Chairman, DMRC was also present along with senior officials. The Central Secretariat station will become a triple interchange station, where the new Magenta Line station will seamlessly connect with the existing Yellow Line and Violet Line. This unique facility will significantly benefit government employees and commuters accessing the Lutyens’ Zone and surrounding administrative districts. The corridor spans 9.913 km with nine underground stations, namely: Shivaji Stadium, Yuge Yugeen Bharat, Central Secretariat, Kartavya Bhawan, India Gate, War Memorial–High Court, Baroda House, Bharat Mandapam, and Indraprastha. This project marks a significant step in strengthening connectivity to the heart of New Delhi, providing efficient access to major government offices, judicial institutions, national memorials, and convention facilities, while enhancing overall network efficiency and passenger convenience.

Every child deserves a childhood. Every child deserves protection. Yet today, thousands of children in Sudan have lost parents, siblings, friends, homes, and access to education. Many are living in refugee and (IDP) camps, carrying memories of war. Thousands of children have been recruited into armed groups and used to serve the interests of commanders, robbing them of their childhood and exposing them to unimaginable #trauma. Children who should be sitting in classrooms reading, playing with friends. The recruitment and use of children in armed conflict is not only devastating, but it is a violation of international law. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) guarantees every child's right to protection, education, survival, and development. At our center, we counsel many of these children. Some tell us How they were recruited into armed groups, How they were treated, and How they were forced to do things that no child should ever be asked to do. Their stories remind us that behind every statistic is a real child whose life has been affected by conflict and who deserves the chance to heal. The world must not look away. Protecting children is not only a moral responsibility, but also a legal obligation under international law. #Sudan #ChildProtection #EndChildRecruitment #ChildrenNotSoldiers #RefugeeChildren #IDPChildren #HumanRights #InternationalLaw #StopTheWarOnChildren

First of all, we discussed the implementation of our plan for long-range sanctions against Russia over this war and the steps needed to bring peace closer. Ukraine’s Defense Forces accurately struck Russian enterprises that produce radio-electronic equipment and other critical components for the needs of the Russian army. Intelligence also obtained internal Russian documents with a real assessment of the consequences of Ukraine’s long-range sanctions. Measures taken by the Russian leadership in response to the situation have also been documented. One such measure is the redeployment of air defense systems from Russian regions to Moscow and to the Kerch Bridge. Basically, these are the two perimeters the Russians have been ordered to protect by weakening other areas on their own territory and in the temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine. We will draw the necessary conclusions. There was a separate report on the state of Russian missile production and strategic military aviation. We are preparing new, entirely just steps in response to Russia prolonging the war and its strikes on Ukrainian territory. It is important that as many Russians as possible come to understand that it is the Russian leadership’s rejection of diplomacy that is prolonging the war. Ukraine has put forward substantive diplomatic proposals. Thank you to everyone who defends our state and our people!

Ambassador Dimitrios Michalopoulos presented his Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat today, marking the assumption of his post as the Ambassador of the Hellenic Republic to ASEAN. Secretary-General Dr. Kao congratulated Ambassador Michalopoulos on his new role and encouraged the Hellenic Republic to explore cooperation with ASEAN, both bilaterally and under the ASEAN-European Union (EU) partnership, in areas of mutual interest, including maritime cooperation, green shipping, disaster management as well as in education, culture and arts. Ambassador Michalopoulos expressed his commitment to fostering engagement between ASEAN and the Hellenic Republic, building on the momentum of the Hellenic Republic’s accession to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) in 2022. He also highlighted the Hellenic Republic’s upcoming Presidency of the Council of the EU in the second half of 2027 as an opportunity to advance the implementation of the EU Indo-Pacific Strategy by strengthening cooperation with regional organisations, particularly ASEAN, while upholding respect for the ASEAN Centrality. The Hellenic Republic appointed its first Ambassador to ASEAN in 2009. Ambassador Michalopoulos succeeds Ambassador Bezirtzoglou, who completed her tenure on 27 September 2025.

And where were some of my friends interrogated, threatened, and placed on house arrest? Inside Al‑Ahli Arab Hospital or the Ma'amadani/Baptist Hospital in Gaza’s Zeitoun neighborhood. Yes, the same hospital that grabbed global headlines early in the war after a faulty Islamic Jihad rocket fell and caused an explosion, which killed hundreds of people. That hospital is now a central hub for Hamas’s intelligence, militancy, and internal repression. This is criminal on every level. And it raises a basic question: if overwhelming, well‑corroborated evidence shows Hamas using Gaza’s medical facilities to hide among civilians and enforce its armed rule, violating the October 2025 ceasefire, why have the UN and international medical and humanitarian NGOs and charities remained silent? Why has no one suspended operations until Hamas withdraws from the hospitals they support? I want every follower and every official who sees this to contact and tag the World Health Organization, UNICEF, UNRWA, the United Nations, Doctors Without Borders, the International Committee of the Red Cross, and any organization supplying Gaza’s hospitals. Demand that they confront Hamas’s presence in the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital/ Ma'amadani / Baptist Hospital and every facility they fund, staff, and sustain. Even though the Episcopal Church/Anglican Diocese of Jerusalem manages Al‑Ahli, every medical facility in Gaza depends on international aid, equipment, and expertise, during the war and even more so since the ceasefire. It is time to get Hamas out of Gaza’s hospitals. It is time to support Gazans risking their lives to protest the Islamist fascists who have destroyed their society for twenty years. And it is time for the international community to finally recognize that Hamas cannot be trusted to uphold any agreement. The group is committed to a last‑stand ideology – much like Hitler in his bunker – regardless of how many civilians in Gaza suffer or die as a result.

कर्नाटक के बीजापुर जिले में स्थित श्री जय वीर हनुमान सांस्कृतिक कला थंडा ने भारत सरकार के संस्कृति मंत्रालय के सहयोग से 10 से 12 फरवरी 2026 को चित्रपिनाकिनी ग्रुप ऑफ एजुकेशनल इंस्टीट्यूशंस, रेड्डी गोल्लारहल्ली में भारत रत्न सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल की 150वीं जयंती पर तीन दिवसीय स्मारक कार्यक्रम आयोजित किया। इस कार्यक्रम का आयोजन सरदार पटेल जी के वर्ष भर चलने वाले स्मरणोत्सव के तहत किया गया। कार्यक्रम की शुरुआत राष्ट्रीय एकता प्रतिज्ञा और आत्मनिर्भर भारत प्रतिज्ञा से हुई। वक्ताओं ने सरदार पटेल के राष्ट्र एकीकरण में योगदान पर जोर देते हुए युवाओं को एकता, अनुशासन और समर्पण के मूल्यों को अपनाने के लिए प्रेरित किया। इस कार्यक्रम में समाज के विभिन्न वर्गों से 3,000 से अधिक लोग शामिल हुए। कार्यक्रम में श्री कृष्ण लीला कन्नड़ नाटक जैसी सांस्कृतिक प्रस्तुतियाँ दी गईं तथा छात्रों को सेमेस्टर पुस्तकें वितरित की गईं। कार्यक्रम का उद्देश्य युवाओं में सरदार पटेल के राष्ट्रीय एकता और राष्ट्र-निर्माण के आदर्शों के प्रति जागरूकता बढ़ाना था। #CultureUnitesAll #150YearsOfSardarPatel

These last 5 days, Ukrainian 🇺🇦 videos showed 193 Russian 🇷🇺 trucks and vehicles hit by drones on key roads. Yesterday, it was 47, today 56, which shows the results of the strikes during the last few weeks. On average, we have nearly 40 trucks destroyed per day this week. This comes amid the intensification of strikes to isolate Crimea, with bridges destroyed, forcing Russian trucks to use pontoon bridges, where they are easier to target. 1/3 of the trucks hit are seemingly "civilian", most with fuel or used by the army. The aim is to slowly cut all logistics. In total since early May, nearly 800 trucks and vehicles have been hit more than 20 km from the frontline, which gives a 15/truck a day average. Remember that you don't need to hit all the trucks to stop the traffic. Russian countermeasures are too few and inefficient to change anything, we've seen numerous mobile fire teams hit or fleeing, with too few examples of successful downing from the ground. Drone interceptors teams are too few and concentrated on key roads, while radars and EW continue to be relentlessly hit. Video Clément Molin (@clement_molin) 3 days later, we have 90 new Russian trucks and vehicles hit by the Ukrainians, which means that the targeting rate is now around 30 a day. Contrary to what I have sometimes read, the mid-range strike campaign is not slowing down and is not suffering from the Russian adaptation thanks to an increase in the number of drones used. I cannot map or gather screeshots for the next 7 days, but the trend will be visible with my next 10 days update (next sunday). Happy Birthday to Nobel Laureate Martin L. Perl! He is famous for discovering a subatomic particle called the tau lepton. In a series of experiments conducted in the mid-1970s at the @SLAClab, Perl and his colleagues used a new particle accelerator to smash electrons and positrons together and observed a phenomenon that could not be explained with the then current scientific knowledge of subatomic particles. The new accelerator was capable of reaching higher energy levels, giving them the ability to detect shorter-lived particles, which Perl named the ‘tau’. This work earned him a share of the @NobelPrize in Physics in 1995.

The 20th Board of Advisers to the ASEAN Committee on Science, Technology and Innovation (COSTI) concluded successfully on 22 June 2026, ahead of the 89th ASEAN COSTI Meeting held on 23 June 2026, in Vientiane, Lao PDR. Both Meetings were hosted by the Ministry of Education and Sports of the Lao PDR. The Board of Advisers (BAC) provides strategic recommendation and independent review to support COSTI in ensuring the effective implementation of the ASEAN Plan of Action on Science, Technology and Innovation (APASTI) 2026–2035. The BAC meeting brought together members from government, academia, and the private sector, while the COSTI Meeting was attended by representatives of all 11 ASEAN Member States and the ASEAN Secretariat, underscoring ASEAN’s collective commitment to strengthening regional STI cooperation and achieving tangible outcomes under APASTI 2026–2035.

Bug Fixes: • Focus reports no longer leak as literal text when split across reads over SSH. • --disable-web-search now honored in grok -p and grok agent; auxiliary model routing respects catalog overrides. • Focus events now fire correctly for SSH-split focus reports. • Boolean tool flags now accept "true"/"false"/"yes"/"no"/1/0 strings and numbers in addition to native booleans. • Session last-active timestamps and message counts no longer regress under concurrent writers. • iTerm2 now always uses text/metadata image fallback instead of broken OSC 1337 overlays. • Model switches no longer leave the prompt queue stuck after a reconnect. • Closing a terminal tab with a running process no longer shows a confirmation dialog. • Custom agent profiles now correctly use the harness required by their pinned model. • Subagents under custom profiles now adopt the correct harness from the parent's model. • Changelog and release-notes modals now scroll with the mouse wheel and arrow keys. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/XFreeze/status/2069299636968591699#m

The butterfly effect. Thirteen years ago, while rounding the Cape of Good Hope, I ran into a bit of a storm. It was also the 540th birthday of Nicolaus Copernicus. Not that there was any connection. It was merely a coincidence of no practical importance. My immediate concerns were existential: to remain within the confines of the boat, keep the bow pointing east and the mast pointing at the sky. The storm became part of the voyage, and the voyage became a story. The story is now part of a school textbook, targeting a group of people who had nothing to do with either the storm or the Cape, but are now forced to read about it. They are the students of Kerala. The latest Plus One English textbook has several pages dedicated to this particular day at the edge of the Atlantic Ocean. As a student, I never regarded textbooks as hurdles. In fact, I always looked forward to the stories in my English textbooks. Finding myself in one is amusing. The last bit may not be a universally shared sentiment, and I imagine many students staring at that chapter and wondering why a sailor couldn’t simply stay ashore and spare everyone the additional reading. A fair question. All I can say in my defence is that I did not plan it that way. The butterfly effect can be a dangerous thing. And it is quite a privilege.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today received the Director- General of the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), Dr. Yvonne Pinto, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat. SG Dr. Kao appreciated IRRI’s 65-year legacy of supporting regional food security and discussed the continued support for the implementation of the Food, Agriculture, and Forestry (FAF) Sectoral Plan 2026–2030. He welcomed IRRI’s new initiative, International Rice Digital Genebank, emphasizing that advanced scientific research must translate into practical, weather-resistant seeds for everyday smallholders. SG Dr. Kao also stressed the importance of data equity to ensure all member states can access these digital tools, while strengthening opportunities for young and women agricultural scientists across the region.

At the invitation of H.E. Assoc. Prof. Dr. Thongsalith Mangnormek, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education and Sports of Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, Secretary-General of ASEAN, will lead the ASEAN Secretariat’s delegation to participate in the 22nd ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Science, Technology and Innovation (AMMSTI-22), to be held in Vientiane, Lao PDR, on 26 June 2026. During the meeting, the Ministers will endorse a landmark restructuring of the ASEAN Committee on Science and Technology and Innovation (COSTI) sub-committee framework from nine to five focused sub-committees, strengthening regional Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) governance, enhancing strategic alignment with ASEAN Plan of Action on Science, Technology and Innovation (APASTI), and enabling impactful delivery of ASEAN STI priorities. The Ministers will also launch of the ASEAN Science, Technology and Innovation Fund (ASTIF) Call 2026, a strategic milestone toward building an inclusive and future-ready regional innovation ecosystem. Anchored on the theme “Advancing ASEAN Plan of Action on Science, Technology and Innovation (APASTI) for a Resilient, Sustainable and Competitive ASEAN,” AMMSTI will set out how resources and partnerships can be mobilised to support an innovation-driven, resilient, sustainable and competitive ASEAN towards the global issue and to advance long-term competitiveness in strategic technologies. On the sidelines of the AMMSTI-22, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn will hold a number of bilateral meetings with ministers from various ASEAN Member States.

Following the signing of the MoU, the previous government received Rs 99.27 crore in SSK funds that had been withheld for not joining the scheme. Everything up to that stage was done by the previous government. The present government has neither signed any new agreement nor taken any further steps so far. The history of the scheme goes back to 2022. On February 24, 2023, Union Education Secretary Sanjay Kumar IAS wrote to the state seeking the signing of an MoU and the selection of schools. In response, then General Education Secretary Rani George IAS sent an assurance letter on March 30, 2024, stating that Kerala was looking forward to establishing PM SHRI schools and that a state-level committee headed by the Principal Secretary, General Education, had been constituted. The letter also said that, based on the committee's recommendations, the MoU would be signed before the 2024-25 academic year. Subsequently, a committee constituted by the previous government examined the issue. In its report dated July 30, 2024, the committee recommended that the PM SHRI scheme could be implemented in Kerala to avoid losing central funds and to ensure that benefits available to students in government schools were not disrupted. It also recommended signing the necessary MoU with the Union Education Ministry. These were decisions and recommendations made during the previous government's tenure" (Pic Source: Sabha TV)

به نظر می‌رسد که حضور گسترده‌ی نیروهای طالبان بیش از آن‌که برای تأمین امنیت عزاداران باشد، برای نظارت بر آنان و جلوگیری از بروز حرکت‌های جمعی و اعتراضی است. همین طالبان تا قبل از تصاحب حکومت، بر مراسم عزاداری شیعیان حملات انتحاری می‌کردند. از جانب دیگر، مراسم عاشورا برای ملاهای شیعه (چهره‌های اصلی مراسم عاشورا) نیز زمینه‌ی اعمال قدرت را فراهم می‌کند. فوکو یادآور می‌شود که قدرت می‌تواند توسط ساختارها و شبکه‌ها اعمال گردد. عزاداری عاشورا مجموعه‌ای از باورها، رفتارها، قاعده‌ها و مناسکی است که یک شبکه را شکل می‌دهند و در درون آن ملا جایگاه ویژه دارد. در واقع، ملاها پایگاه اجتماعی‌شان را مدیون همین شبکه‌ اند. از این‌رو برای ملاهای شیعه مراسم عاشورا یک شبکه‌ی اعمال قدرت است. در جامعه‌ی فعلی هزاره‌ها ملاها به‌رغم این‌که مناصب رسمی-دولتی ندارند، پایگاه اجتماعی بالایی دارند و از توانایی بسیج نیروی اجتماعی برخوردار هستند. این قدرت ملاهای شیعه نه با پولیس یا زندان بلکه به‌وسیله‌ی همین مراسم عزاداری اعمال می‌گردد. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/256130/sunni-…

At Swallow Rock in Lianhua Mountain in Guangzhou, an ancient quarry has transformed into a serene landscape of striking beauty. Towering cliffs stand above clear green waters, their reddish surfaces softened by trailing vines and lush vegetation. Once a stone quarry of the ancient Nanyue people over 2,000 years ago, it now blends human history with nature's quiet restoration — where old chisel marks meet living greenery. The site dates back to the Nanyue (204-111 BC) period, when the Nanyue people lived in the Lingnan region (a region in southern China covering Guangdong, Guangxi, Hainan, Hong Kong and Macao). NITI Aayog released the eighth edition of Trade Watch Quarterly (Q4 FY 2025-26) on 23 June 2026 in New Delhi. Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog, released the Eighth edition of Trade Watch Quarterly for Q4 FY’2025-26, in the presence of other senior officials. The analysis highlights India’s resilient trade performance in Q4 FY 2025-26, supported by robust growth in services exports. While merchandise exports moderated by 2.8% to USD 112.0 billion and imports rose by 11.9% to USD 195.5 billion, services exports grew by 9.0% to USD 111.1 billion, sustaining a strong services surplus. Overall, India’s total trade reached USD 1.84 trillion during FY 2025-26, with exports growing by 4.2% and imports by 6.5%, alongside continued diversification in trade markets. This quarter’s thematic focus is on pharmaceuticals, a key pillar of India’s manufacturing and export ecosystem. With global pharmaceutical and API import demand estimated at USD 1.3 trillion in 2025 and India’s exports reaching USD 35.8 billion, the sector is well-positioned to strengthen its global footprint. The analysis highlights opportunities in biologics, biosimilars, vaccines and advanced therapeutics, alongside the need to enhance innovation, research and development, domestic API capabilities and regulatory cooperation to improve competitiveness and supply-chain resilience. Delighted to welcome my dear brother, President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian of the Islamic Republic of Iran, to Pakistan today. This was our first meeting after the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum and the first round of technical talks in Burgenstock. DPM Ishaq Dar and Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, were also present, alongwith senior Cabinet members and government officials. We held warm and most cordial discussions wherein we reaffirmed our shared commitment to regional peace and the importance of pursuing dialogue and diplomacy to resolve all outstanding issues. We also agreed to further strengthen the enduring Pakistan-Iran relationship and expand cooperation across all areas of mutual interest. I conveyed Pakistan’s deep appreciation for the wise and sagacious leadership of His Eminence Supreme Leader Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, and paid tribute to my dear brother President Pezeshkian and the Iranian leadership for guiding their brave and resilient nation with honour, patience and dignity during a challenging period. I thanked the Iranian leadership for reposing its abiding trust in Pakistan as a sincere friend, neighbour and mediator. Pakistan remains committed to working closely with Iran for the peace, progress and prosperity of our two nations and the broader region.

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif warmly welcomed Iranian President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian and his delegation to Pakistan amid reaffirming Islamabad’s commitment to strengthening bilateral ties across multiple sectors, including trade, economic development, infrastructure and reconstruction, and promoting peace and stability in the region. During his opening remarks at the delegation-level talks, the Prime Minister said it was a great pleasure to receive the Iranian President in Islamabad and thanked him for accepting his invitation to visit Pakistan. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said, “I have no doubt that the brave and resilient people of Iran, with their immense capabilities and natural resources, will transform their country into a flourishing economy.” Pakistan and Iran would continue joint efforts to achieve shared prosperity, he added. The prime minister thanked the Iranian leadership for trusting Pakistan’s sincere and honest mediation efforts and assured Tehran that Pakistan would continue to play a constructive role in promoting lasting peace. “True brotherhood requires no questions or answers,” the Prime Minister remarked, emphasizing that Pakistan would continue supporting peace initiatives based on dignity, honour and mutual respect. The prime minister conveyed his warm regards to Iran’s Supreme Leader and praised the Iranian leadership for its efforts that led to the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) and the achievement of a ceasefire with “dignity and honour.” Expressing solidarity with the people of Iran, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif offered his deepest condolences over the loss of innocent lives, including children, women, boys and girls, during the recent conflict. He commended President Pezeshkian’s sagacious, calm and vigilant leadership that had helped pave the way for a more peaceful future. Highlighting the role of Pakistan’s military leadership, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif particularly acknowledged the efforts of Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, whom he credited with working tirelessly to facilitate dialogue and support the signing of the MoU. “He worked untiringly through difficult days and nights with one mission: to do everything humanly possible to stop a war that could have brought devastation across vast regions,” the prime minister said. He also referred to the first technical-level session held in Switzerland and thanked Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Ishaq Dar as well as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi for their diplomatic engagements and shuttle diplomacy efforts. The prime minister further appreciated the support extended by Qatar and other brotherly countries for advancing the peace initiative. He also lauded the contributions of Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi for their support and efforts toward regional stability. PM Shehbaz Sharif noted that he had informed Parliament about President Pezeshkian’s visit and said the people of Pakistan were delighted to welcome the Iranian leader. Reaffirming the close ties between the two neighbouring countries, he stated, “Iran and Pakistan are brothers, and we stand together in times of happiness and sorrow.” Addressing speculation regarding the contents of the MoU, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif clarified that ballistic missiles were neither included in the agreement nor discussed during negotiations, as the issue was not on the agenda. He cautioned against any misunderstanding regarding the agreement and suggested that certain elements had attempted to undermine peace efforts. The prime minister emphasized that there should be no confusion about the MoU’s scope, reiterating that it focused on promoting peace and stability and did not contain any provisions related to ballistic missile issues. 1. In this season of mass defections, all to the BJP, 3 interconnected political questions arise. Why do parties break up? Why do individuals defect? Do ideology, principle, even loyalty, matter? All of these then lead to a central logical question: Why do some parties break up, or haemorrhage fatally, but some don’t? I analyse these in my latest #NationalInterest. 2. Let’s first check out the broad scoresheet over these months of high ‘mobility’. The destruction of Mamata’s TMC has been the standout headline. But there’s competition — Shiv Sena (UBT), Jharkhand INDIA MLAs cross-voting, members of AAP, BJD, YSRCP, Akali Dal, and, of course, the Congress all defecting. 3. It will be said that BJP is a magnet for the losers from all parties because that’s where the spoils are. Further, that the BJP employs saam, daam, dand, bhed to break rivals. Its laundromat politics is key to this one-way movement. For engineering mass defections, the BJP has perfected the doctrine of the split: Get two-thirds to move and say you’re the real party. 4. So, why do most parties break, but some don’t? I would list only 3 that don’t. The BJP, SP, & the Left spectrum. The Leftists had many arguments & splits but stayed together in one front. Commitment to ideology indeed is the glue that keeps parties together. The Left is today completely out of power, at the lowest point in its history, but nobody is even exploring elsewhere. 5. The BJP-Left cohesion through lifetimes of wilderness is matched by the SP that Mulayam Singh Yadav founded. Of all the OBC-Muslim vote bank parties post 1992 it’s been the most durable. It has a fairly clear ideology & Akhilesh has kept his vote banks’ trust. So, there’s a belief that one day power could return. The political force chewing on this should be the Congress. 6. The self-righteous Europeans who don't want to install AC are literally killing their grandparents and other vulnerable people Tony Aubé (@aubetony) After a hellish week in a Paris Airbnb with no AC (100°F outside, 108°F+ inside), I started looking into why the French are so opposed to AC. There's many reasons: bureaucracy, poverty, etc. But the main one is decades of environmental campaigns that convinced people AC is the devil. The result? You can't escape the heat. Most buses, metro lines, and shopping malls have no AC. This Monday, 850 schools are closing because classroom temperatures exceed 104°F. In Nantes, they built a brand-new train station and a hospital without AC for environmental reasons. The station is now partially closed because it's become a "furnace" that endangers travelers. Hospitals are covering windows with emergency foil blankets to protect patients. The French demonize air conditioning because it creates carbon emissions that contribute to climate change. Never mind that France already has one of most carbon-free electricity in the world thanks to nuclear, or that it accounts for less than 1% of global emissions. They also oppose AC because it "just displace the problem" by dumping heat into the street. Never mind that studies suggest even if an entire city were air-conditioned, the increase in outdoor temperature would be at most about 1°F. Instead, people are willing to endure 104°F+ indoors to avoid a marginal increase outdoors. This ideology kills more people than firearms in the United States. Across Europe, between 50,000 and 70,000 people die from heat every year, mostly the elderly and the poor. Compare that to roughly 44,000 Americans killed by firearms. For comparison, despite having a similar population, deserts, and more extreme temperatures, the United States has only about 2,500 heat-related deaths per year thanks to widespread AC. That's what bothers me most. The moralizing posture completely detached from reality. People feel morally superior for "not polluting." They criticize America and its guns while tolerating policies that kills even more people. I share this anecdote because I know it's shocking to Americans. Here, schools or hospitals reaching 104°F would be unnaceptable. The absurdity is immediately obvious to us because we're looking from the outside. We see the gap between moral intentions and real-world consequences. But we're no different. In America, we have dozens of similar issues where we're just as irrational, and we've become blind to them because the solution isn't politically acceptable. There was so much noise around the Telecom Amendment Bill because we lacked understanding of its purpose and vision. A very informative conversation on ZHK where @aamir_ibrahim01 was invited who explained the purpose and its vision. @ZarrarKhuhro @WusatUllahKhan Aamir Hafeez Ibrahim (@aamir_ibrahim01) The debate around the Telecom Amendment Bill is welcome. However, much of the discussion has overlooked the central issue the proposed Right of Way amendments are intended to address. Pakistan’s connectivity challenges are, at their core, infrastructure challenges. Fiber cannot be laid, towers cannot be deployed, and networks cannot be expanded without resolving the Right of Way bottlenecks that have frustrated operators and slowed digital progress for years. These are not abstract regulatory concerns - they translate directly into slower deployment, weaker coverage, and underserved communities. The proposed amendments seek to address this long-standing challenge by creating a clearer and more predictable framework for telecom infrastructure deployment. Much of the current criticism has been driven by the perception that the reforms are aimed at individual citizens and homeowners. That is not the intent of the proposal. The objective is to address barriers that have slowed infrastructure rollout and limited connectivity expansion. As with any legislation, the language can and should be refined through the parliamentary process. Legitimate concerns should be debated, improvements should be considered, and the final law should be strengthened through that process. But the broader objective should not be lost. Expanding connectivity requires investment, infrastructure deployment, and regulatory frameworks that support both. In that regard, the effort to address long-standing Right of Way challenges is both necessary and overdue. পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রামে বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনীর চিকিৎসা সহায়তা ও বৃক্ষরোপণ কর্মসূচি ঢাকা, ২৩ জুন ২০২৬ (মঙ্গলবার): পার্বত্য চট্টগ্রামের বিভিন্ন এলাকায় বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনীর উদ্যোগে মানবিক কার্যক্রমের অংশ হিসেবে বিনামূল্যে চিকিৎসা সহায়তা প্রদান এবং পরিবেশ সংরক্ষণের লক্ষ্যে বৃক্ষরোপণ কর্মসূচির আওতায় গাছের চারা বিতরণ করা হয়েছে। আজ রাঙ্গামাটি রিজিয়নের জুরাছড়ি জোন কর্তৃক আয়োজিত চিকিৎসা ক্যাম্পেইনের মাধ্যমে স্থানীয় ১২০ জন পাহাড়ি ও ৮০ জন বাঙালি চিকিৎসাপ্রার্থীকে বিনামূল্যে প্রয়োজনীয় চিকিৎসা সেবা ও ঔষধ প্রদান করা হয়। অপরদিকে, একই দিনে বান্দরবান রিজিয়নের আলীকদম জোনের উদ্যোগে বৃক্ষরোপন কর্মসূচির আওতায় আলীকদম সরকারি উচ্চ বিদ্যালয় এবং সেন্ট মেরিস স্কুলের শিক্ষার্থীদের মাঝে ৪,০০০ টি বিভিন্ন প্রজাতির ফলজ, বনজ ও ঔষধি গাছের চারা বিতরণ করা হয়। পাশাপাশি, উভয় শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান প্রাঙ্গণে স্থানীয় গণ্যমান্য ব্যক্তিবর্গ ও অতিথিগণের উপস্থিতিতে বৃক্ষরোপণ করা হয়। উল্লেখ্য, সবুজায়ন ও পরিবেশের ভারসাম্য রক্ষার উদ্দেশ্যে এই এলাকায় সেনাবাহিনীর উদ্যোগে এ বছর বিভিন্ন প্রজাতির ৬৫,০০০ গাছের চারা রোপনের কর্মপরিকল্পনা গ্রহণ করা হয়েছে। সামাজিক দায়বদ্ধতার অংশ হিসেবে বাংলাদেশ সেনাবাহিনী পার্বত্য অঞ্চলে মানবিক সহায়তা, পরিবেশ সংরক্ষণ ও জনকল্যাণমূলক কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করে আসছে এবং ভবিষ্যতে এ ধারা অব্যাহত থাকবে।

Residents of all JJ clusters established in Delhi up to January 1, 2025 will now be eligible for rehabilitation benefits. This historic decision, taken at the 36th meeting of the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board (DUSIB) chaired by Chief Minister Smt. Rekha Gupta, is in line with the Delhi Slum and JJ Rehabilitation and Relocation Policy, 2026 finalised under the guidance of Hon’ble Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah. Until now, 2015 served as the cut-off year for rehabilitation. By extending the eligibility to January 1, 2025, this decision will bring lakhs of slum-dwelling families within the ambit of rehabilitation and renewed hope. The decision advances Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi commitment to the welfare of the poor and opens the path to modern housing with schools, health centres, anganwadis, playgrounds and other essential amenities, enabling families to live with dignity and security. #ViksitDelhi

Assented to the Finance Bill, 2026, and the Appropriation Bill, 2026, which provide the legal framework and resources required to finance our transformation priorities, create jobs, strengthen livelihoods and invest in the future. The Finance Act, 2026, does not raise taxes. Instead, it improves fairness by strengthening compliance, closing loopholes and ensuring that every individual and business pays what is lawfully due. We are pursuing tax avoidance, not taxpayers; offshore schemes, not ordinary wages; and leakages, not livelihoods. Contrary to misinformation, there are no taxes on freehold land, no taxes on mitumba, no changes to rental income tax, no tax on bottled water, no new tax on M-PESA or mobile money transactions, no new tax on mobile airtime or data, and no new tax on locally manufactured packaging for essential products. The Sultanate of Oman and the Islamic Republic of Iran held discussions in Muscat during the visit of H.E. Dr. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and H.E. Dr. Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs. The Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed its support to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding signed between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran and the importance of sustaining dialogue and coordination in support of its successful implementation. The Islamic Republic of Iran and the Sultanate of Oman as the Coastal States of the Strait of Hormuz, reaffirm their commitment to the safe passage through the Strait, in line with applicable international law, while emphasizing their sovereignty and sovereign rights over their territorial waters in the Strait of Hormuz.The two sides discussed matters relating to the Strait of Hormuz, in accordance with the provisions of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. In this context, they have also agreed to hold discussions with the littoral States in the region, and with any other relevant parties. All arrangements related to the Strait of Hormuz must fully respect the sovereignty and sovereign rights of the two Coastal States of the Strait. The Sultanate of Oman and the Islamic Republic of Iran reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining the Strait of Hormuz as a secure and open waterway for international navigation. 1. Tamil Nadu’s new TVK govt has released a White Paper on the state’s finances for the 5 post-Covid years, which coincide with DMK rule. It compares the state with 3 peers — Gujarat, Maharashtra & Karnataka. #CutTheClutter analyses the data & conclusions presented & looks at how welfare-driven politics has impacted the state’s economy & what it could mean for the future. 2. First, the debt situation. And it’s a headline you’ve all seen: A child born in Tamil Nadu carries a debt burden Rs 1.28L. The state’s outstanding debt has doubled in 5 years — from Rs 5.13 lakh crore in 2020-21 to nearly Rs 10 lakh crore in 2025-26. If you add guarantees & contingent liabilities, total obligations rise to Rs 13.18 lakh crore. 3. Tamil Nadu’s debt-to-GDP ratio (28.3%) has remained elevated throughout while the 3 other states in the peer group have managed to reduce it. This, the White Paper says, makes the challenge tougher for Tamil Nadu because it also has a demographic challenge — too few children are being born, & it’s the oldest state in India at a mean age of 34.5 years. 4. Interest payments now consume 23% of all of Tamil Nadu’s income. But when it comes to the state’s own tax revenue, 35% of that goes towards interest payments. How? Because, besides SOTR, Tamil Nadu also gets a share of Central taxes & grants. Annual interest payment right now is 1/3rd more than capital expenditure. Tamil Nadu, therefore, is spending more on servicing its existing debt than on creating assets. This is the classical debt trap. 5. Tamil Nadu’s revenue deficit stands at ₹78,324 crore (2.2% of GSDP). In simple terms: the state’s regular income is insufficient even to cover its regular expenses. So, it is borrowing to fund consumption, not investment. The govt’s committed expenditures (salaries, pensions & interest) are the highest among all peers. If you pay all of that, then in Tamil Nadu’s budget there is no headroom left for any capital expenditure. 6. Nearly all state PSUs are making losses, the biggest are the power PSUs. But these survive because govt guarantees their borrowing, which has created an intergenerational burden. Fiscal deficit is now expected to be Rs 1.64 lakh crore. So, the maximum the state can borrow is Rs 1.52 lakh crore. It can borrow a little more for its power utilities. Even so, it will be left with Rs 11,600 crore of unfilled deficit. Where will that come from? 7. watch #CutTheClutter: Tamil Nadu debt, deficits & welfare: What Vijay's White Paper says about Stalin govt’s finances ￼ youtube.com/watch?v=hKd74U9a…

PHOTO | Andhra Pradesh: The State Cabinet has taken a key decision benefiting government employees. It approved increasing the retirement age of employees working in Public Sector Undertakings from 60 to 62 years. The Cabinet took this decision to raise the retirement age for employees and teachers of various state government PSUs, Gurukuls, and societies. The Cabinet meeting agreed to increase the retirement age from 60 to 62 years for employees working in PSUs, employees and teachers working in SC, ST, BC, Minority Welfare Societies, and employees and teachers working in Gurukul schools, on par with state government employees. The State Cabinet decided to extend the Old Pension Scheme to employees appointed through various notifications issued before September 2004. With Cabinet approval, 11,000 employees will move from the Contributory Pension Scheme to the Old Pension Scheme. The government’s decision will ensure financial and social security for employees post-retirement. Chief Minister Chandrababu clarified that the coalition people’s government will stand by all employees. (Source: Third Party) #AndhraPradesh

NITI Aayog released the eighth edition of Trade Watch Quarterly (Q4 FY 2025-26) on 23 June 2026 in New Delhi. Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog, released the Eighth edition of Trade Watch Quarterly for Q4 FY’2025-26, in the presence of other senior officials. The analysis highlights India’s resilient trade performance in Q4 FY 2025-26, supported by robust growth in services exports. While merchandise exports moderated by 2.8% to USD 112.0 billion and imports rose by 11.9% to USD 195.5 billion, services exports grew by 9.0% to USD 111.1 billion, sustaining a strong services surplus. Overall, India’s total trade reached USD 1.84 trillion during FY 2025-26, with exports growing by 4.2% and imports by 6.5%, alongside continued diversification in trade markets. This quarter’s thematic focus is on pharmaceuticals, a key pillar of India’s manufacturing and export ecosystem. With global pharmaceutical and API import demand estimated at USD 1.3 trillion in 2025 and India’s exports reaching USD 35.8 billion, the sector is well-positioned to strengthen its global footprint. The analysis highlights opportunities in biologics, biosimilars, vaccines and advanced therapeutics, alongside the need to enhance innovation, research and development, domestic API capabilities and regulatory cooperation to improve competitiveness and supply-chain resilience. With demand for critical minerals rising rapidly due to electric mobility and energy storage, AI Infrastructure and other emerging technologies, recycling must be viewed not only as an environmental imperative but also as a strategic economic opportunity. Continued innovation, industry participation and policy support will be key to building a robust and resilient critical minerals recycling ecosystem in India.

The discussions highlighted the critical role of recycling in strengthening India’s resource security and supporting its clean energy and technology ambitions. While significant opportunities exist, scaling the sector will require addressing challenges related to robust system of continuous feedstock availability, economic viability of processing and recovery technologies, integration of recovered materials into industrial value chains, and coordination across multiple ministries and stakeholders that shape the ecosystem.

राज्यातील सर्वाधिक मूल्य असलेल्या पिकांच्या नैसर्गिक आपत्तीत होणाऱ्या नुकसानीची अचूक आकडेवारी मिळविण्यासाठी आगामी कालावधीत कृषी आणि आपत्ती व्यवस्थापन यांनी संयुक्तरित्या ड्रोन सर्वेक्षण करण्यासाठी प्रशासनाने केलेली नोंद तपासून घ्यावी. रियल टाइम डेटा, महाराष्ट्र रिमोट सेन्सिंग ॲप्लिकेशन सेंटरचा डेटा आणि सॅटेलाइट डेटा तपासून घेऊन तात्काळ भरपाईची कार्यवाही करावी असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी या बैठकीत दिले. राज्य शासनाने शेतकऱ्यांच्या संरक्षणासाठी पीकविमा योजनांमध्ये मोठ्या प्रमाणावर आर्थिक सहभाग नोंदविला आहे, त्यामुळे पात्र शेतकऱ्यांना कोणताही त्रास होणार नाही याची दक्षता विमा कंपन्यांनी घेण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी दिले. त्याचवेळी गैरप्रकारांना आळा घालण्यासाठी अत्याधुनिक तंत्रज्ञानाचा वापर करून पडताळणी प्रक्रिया अधिक मजबूत करण्यात यावी. जळगाव وزارت خارجه‌ی طالبان اعلام کرده است که هیأت این گروه گفت‌وگوهای دوجانبه‌ی خود را با کشورهای عضو اتحادیه اروپا در بروکسل به پایان رسانده است. عبدالقهار بلخی، سخن‌گوی وزارت خارجه‌ی طالبان شام امروز (سه‌شنبه، ۲ سرطان) با نشر اعلامیه‌ای گفته است که این هیأت را او رهبری کرده است. او افزوده است که آنان با کشورهای عضو اتحادیه اروپا در مورد ازسرگیری خدمات قنسولی به شهروندان افغانستان در اروپا، اعتمادسازی، حضور مؤثر و راه‌های حل مشکلات افغان‌هایی که درخواست پناهندگی آنان در اروپا پذیرفته نشده و با مشکلات متعدد روبه‌رو هستند، گفت‌وگو کرده‌اند. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/256104

اتحادیه اروپا اعلام کرده است که ۲۰ میلیون یورو برای کمک به بازگشت‌کنندگان و آوارگان در افغانستان از طریق سازمان بین‌المللی مهاجرت، اختصاص می‌دهد. نمایندگی اتحادیه اروپا در کابل امروز (سه‌شنبه، ۲ سرطان) با نشر اعلامیه‌ای گفته است که این حمایت مالی در زمانی صورت می‌گیرد که افغانستان همچنان یکی از بزرگ‌ترین و پیچیده‌ترین بحران‌های انسانی جهان را تجربه می‌کند و با تعداد بالای بازگشت‌ها، این بحران تشدید شده است. ورونیکا بوسکویچ پوهار، سرپرست نمایندگی اتحادیه اروپا در افغانستان گفته است: «اتحادیه اروپا همچنان به تعهد خود برای حمایت از ادغام مجدد بازگشت‌کنندگان در افغانستان پابند است و به آنان در گذار از وابستگی به خودکفایی کمک می‌کند.» بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/256101

I was pleased to welcome OECD Secretary-General @MathiasCormann to Kyiv today. We discussed the latest developments on the battlefield, the consequences of Russia’s continued attacks against Ukraine’s people, energy infrastructure, and economy, as well as broader security developments in our region. Despite the war, Ukraine continues to advance on its path toward the EU and OECD, implementing reforms and strengthening institutions. We reviewed cooperation under OECD programmes, Ukraine’s advancement in meeting OECD standards and criteria, and the Organization’s valuable contribution to our reform and modernization efforts. We highly value the OECD’s reviews on infrastructure, public governance, and justice policies to be presented today. These are practical tools that strengthen Ukraine’s resilience and reforms. We also discussed preparations for the Ukraine Recovery Conference and the importance of mobilizing international support for Ukraine’s recovery, resilience, and long-term development. I thanked the OECD for its principled support for Ukraine and look forward to further progress on Ukraine’s path toward OECD accession, including a positive decision by the OECD Council on opening accession discussions and adopting an Accession Roadmap.

To reach people left behind, health systems need both evidence and trust. This is what WHO/Europe and the Council of European Bishops’ Conferences (CCEE) are seeking to bring together through the Letter of Intent I signed today with CCEE President Archbishop Gintaras Grušas. The signing follows our pastoral health-care conference at the Vatican in March, which brought together Catholic institutions from 45 countries. His Holiness Pope Leo XIV reminded us at that meeting, “Health cannot be a luxury for the few. It is an essential condition for social peace.” These words speak directly to the purpose of our cooperation: reducing health inequities, promoting mental health, addressing loneliness, responding to climate-related health risks, and strengthening dialogue rooted in dignity and trust. The need is urgent. Across the European Region, 19 million young people are struggling to build secure and healthy lives. 99 million working-age adults face higher risks of stress, anxiety and depression. 34 million older people are at greater risk of strokes, dementia and falls, often linked to poor housing, unsafe neighbourhoods and social isolation. Behind these numbers are people who need support earlier, closer to home and in ways they can trust, and this is where our cooperation will make a practical difference.

President Droupadi Murmu presents Padma Bhushan to Dr. Vijay Amritraj for his exceptional contribution to the field of Sports. One of the greatest tennis players of India, he represented the country in the Davis Cup for 20 consecutive years. He achieved a career-high ATP ranking of 16, the highest by an Indian. He won 16 ATP Tour singles titles, which is the highest by any Asian player. In 2001, he was appointed a United Nations Messenger of Peace, the only Indian athlete to receive that distinction.

President Droupadi Murmu presents Padma Vibhushan to Justice (Retd.) K. T. Thomas for his exceptional contribution to the field of Public Affairs. A retired Judge of the Supreme Court of India, Shri Thomas is known for his contribution to criminal law, police reforms and the fight against corruption. He has headed the first committee in India to complete the work of fixing fees for 200 colleges. As Chairman of various Committees and Commissions at state and national levels, he made recommendations on various issues. Justice (Retd.) Thomas was conferred Padma Bhushan in 2007.

President Droupadi Murmu presents Padma Vibhushan to Shri P. Narayanan for his exceptional contribution to the field of Literature and Education. Shri Narayanan, popularly known as Narayanji, has dedicated his life to nationalistic journalism and socio-political organization in Kerala. He led the daily Janmabhumi since its inception in 1975. His weekly column Sanghapadhathiloode became a historical record, chronicling the lives of unsung volunteers who suffered state excesses during the Emergency.

A herd of wild elephants in Assam, a Northeastern state in India, were crossing a railway track and were spotted by the co-pilots of the approaching Rajdhani Express, a super-fast passenger train. Loco Pilot S.N. Raju and Assistant Loco Pilot R.K. Singh displayed admirable reflexes by hitting the train’s emergency brakes in time. Their alertness prevented a possible collision, allowing the elephant herd to cross safely between Titabar and Mariani, two small neighbouring railway stations in Assam. The migration of wild elephants has raised many concerns for the animals’ safety in different parts of the country, mainly the forest areas of Coimbatore and West Bengal. In many cases, elephants have been killed by train collisions. Video

Lew Anno Support#USA#NATO#Ukraine 24/2-22 (@anno1540) 1/2 KINBURN SPIT: RUSSIA'S POSITION MAY BE COLLAPSING For nearly four years Russia maintained a military presence on the Kinburn Spit despite extreme logistical difficulties. The narrow strip of land at the entrance to the Dnipro-Bug estuary has strategic value far beyond its size. Whoever controls Kinburn influences access to the ports of Mykolaiv and Kherson and can threaten maritime traffic across a large section of Ukraine's southern coastline. Now there are growing indications that Russia's position on the spit has become increasingly difficult to sustain. The most significant development is that Ukrainian military command has officially confirmed that Russian logistics on the spit have been severely disrupted. Colonel Denys Nosikov, commander of the Operational Tactical Group "Odesa," stated that Ukrainian forces have "practically cut off" Russian supply routes. According to Nosikov, deliveries of ammunition, fuel, food, and water have effectively stopped. His assessment is straightforward: "A soldier cannot fight without food and fresh water." According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russian forces are now being evacuated from positions on the spit. This statement is particularly important because it represents the first official confirmation from Ukrainian military command that an evacuation may be underway. The development follows earlier reports from the partisan movement Atesh, which on June 8 claimed that elements of Russia's 337th Airborne Assault Regiment had begun withdrawing from parts of the Kinburn area. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif addresses the National Assembly Session (23 June, 2026).

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed confidence that the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Iran and the United States would evolve into a long-term agreement following 60 days of technical-level dialogue, helping ensure peace and stability across the world. Addressing the National Assembly, the prime minister congratulated the nation on a historic development, saying that the MoU had been signed by Iran and the United States, with Pakistan serving as a mediator. "It is a historic moment that Pakistan signed the MoU as a mediator between Iran and the United States," he remarked. The prime minister informed the House that the leadership of both countries participated in a high-level committee meeting in Burgenstock, Switzerland, a couple of days ago. He said Pakistan made sincere efforts to facilitate dialogue and reconciliation between the two sides, resulting in the preparation of a joint statement. He said a ceasefire between Iran and the United States had come into effect and that technical-level talks would continue over the next 60 days. Congratulating the nation, Shehbaz Sharif described Pakistan's role in securing the truce as historic, adding that the country's efforts had received widespread recognition in international media. "The respect Pakistan has earned around the world through this achievement could not have been bought even by spending billions," he said. The prime minister also informed the House that Iranian President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian was scheduled to arrive in Islamabad later in the day, where discussions would be held on further expanding bilateral cooperation between the two countries. Referring to remarks made by Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai in the National Assembly, the prime minister said all four provinces had contributed to the development of Balochistan, which he termed a matter of satisfaction. He reiterated his longstanding view that Pakistan could not achieve sustainable economic development unless all four provinces progressed equally. Video

Those who have sinister agendas may try to twist them but they cannot take Kashmir out of me or out from Pakistan or take Pakistan out of Kashmir. The sacrifices of Kashmiris who crossed over into Pakistan in October 1947 are recorded in history, etched in their memory forever. The struggle of Kashmiris in Indian-Occupied Kashmir against Indian occupation is a saga of martyrdom and lives spent in jails over the last 78 years. Pakistan’s commitment to the Kashmir cause is witnessed in the blood of our martyrs in five wars, and in our principaled stand on a plebiscite and self determination as per UN resolutions. In this backdrop, the nefarious and external agenda driven voices coming out of AJK against Pakistan and the Kashmir cause must be responded to in the strongest possible terms. There are Kashmiris who paid the price for migration, and those who continue to pay the price in IIOJK. आज श्री मुक्तसर साहिब में शिक्षा मंत्री हरजोत बैंस जी के साथ Punjab Bright Minds कार्यक्रम के तहत सीबीएसई और पीएसईबी में अपने ज़िले में टॉप करने वाले विद्यार्थियों से संवाद किया। इस संवाद के दौरान मुक्तसर साहिब के एक छोटे से गाँव के बच्चे ने जब कहा कि पिछले साढ़े चार साल में उसके स्कूल की सुविधाएँ ऐसी हो गई हैं कि उसे वो change, innovation कनाडा के स्कूलों जैसे लगते हैं, इसलिए उसका स्कूल जाने का मन करता है। यह सुनकर लगा कि हाँ.. राजनीति में आकर ठीक ही किया, क्योंकि जिस सोच के साथ हम राजनीति में आए थे, वह सोच आज पंजाब के गाँव-गाँव तक पहुँच गई है। क्योंकि ये बच्चे वो हैं, जिनके मन में पंजाब और भारत को लेकर बड़े सपने हैं और उन सपनों को सच कर दिखाने का जज़्बा भी है। उनसे बातचीत करते हुए बात बार-बार सामने आई कि जिन सपनों की उड़ान वे भरना चाहते हैं, उनके लिए बच्चों को आम आदमी पार्टी की सरकार ज़रूरी लगती है।

Residents of all JJ clusters established in Delhi up to January 1, 2025 will now be eligible for rehabilitation benefits. C’est dans cette géométrie que les transferts houthis de drones iraniens vers des groupes islamistes soudanais prennent leur pleine signification stratégique. Il ne s’agit pas d’un phénomène de prolifération périphérique mais d’une manœuvre de consolidation d’un arc de présence allant du Yémen à l’Afrique sub-saharienne. Sudanest en train de devenir le poste d’écoute de Téhéran en face des mouvements navals américains, saoudiens et émiratis, pont entre le nord arabe et l’intérieur africain, potentiellement vers le Sahel. Si les négociations de Bürgenstock aboutissent à un accord nucléaire contraignant l’Iran à réduire le soutien à ses proxies, la question de la pérennité de cette architecture africaine, moins visible, moins directement contrainte par les termes d’un éventuel accord, deviendra l’un des angles morts majeurs de la diplomatie post-guerre.

Du côté israélo-occidental, la réponse suit une logique symétrique. Tandis que la guerre contre l’Iran fait rage, Israël planifie discrètement une présence potentielle à Berbera, en Somaliland, à l’embouchure de la mer Rouge, pour frapper l’un des derniers proxies iraniens (bien qu’ayant une démarche plus transactionnelle et autonome) encore opérant à pleine capacité : les Houthis du Yémen. Cette présence en gestation s’inscrit dans un «axe de Berbera» combinant les intérêts sécuritaires israéliens, les investissements infrastructurels émiratis et les ambitions maritimes éthiopiennes, faisant de Berbera un hub stratégique en cours de militarisation croissante. Face à cet axe, se dessine un «axe du statu quo» regroupant l’Arabie saoudite, l’Égypte et la Turquie, qui cherche à préserver la souveraineté nominale des États côtiers, notamment pour protéger les projets d’infrastructure ( notamment turcs) à Port-Soudan.

✍️ #THREAD | La guerre des axes stratégiques se dessine en mer Rouge La configuration qui se dessine au Soudan ne peut se lire isolément : elle constitue l’un des nœuds d’une bataille de positionnement stratégique qui structure désormais l’ensemble du corridor mer Rouge–Bab el-Mandeb. Du côté iranien, la logique est celle d’un encerclement progressif de la péninsule arabique par les flancs. Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, today met with Ms. Kanni Wignaraja, United Nations Assistant Secretary-General and UNDP Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat. The discussion highlighted ongoing engagement and exchanged views on future cooperation in areas including sustainable development, blue economy, sustainable finance, innovation, and regional resilience, and explored ways to further strengthen the ASEAN–UNDP partnership in support of inclusive and sustainable growth across the region.

Ambassador of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka to ASEAN, H.E. Sashikala Premawardhane, presented her Letter of Credence (LOC) to the Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat, today. Secretary-General Dr. Kao congratulated Ambassador Premawardhane on her appointment as Ambassador of Sri Lanka to ASEAN and looked forward to working closely with her to further enhance ASEAN-Sri Lanka relations. He commended Sri Lanka for its active participation in ASEAN-led mechanisms, particularly the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), and encouraged Sri Lanka to promote its engagement with ASEAN through the frameworks of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA). He also encouraged Sri Lanka to explore opportunities for cooperation with ASEAN in areas of mutual interest, including maritime cooperation, trade, investment, tourism, business-to-business linkages, connectivity, sustainable development, education, disaster management, and people-to-people exchanges. Ambassador Premawardhane expressed Sri Lanka’s commitment to enhancing its engagement with ASEAN and the ASEAN Member States and underlined Sri Lanka’s interest in further strengthening cooperation with ASEAN. Ambassador Premawardhane also highlighted the work Sri Lanka has undertaken within the ARF framework, particularly in the areas of non-proliferation and disarmament, disaster relief, and defence education, and reiterated Sri Lanka’s keen interest in pursuing ASEAN’s Sectoral Dialogue Partnership Status. She looked forward to working closely with the ASEAN Secretariat and ASEAN Member States in identifying possible cooperation areas of mutual interest. Sri Lanka acceded to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) in 2007 and accredited its first Ambassador to ASEAN in 2016. Ambassador Premawardhane is the fourth Ambassador of Sri Lanka to ASEAN and succeeds Ambassador Admiral (Prof.) Jayanath Siri Kumara Colombage, who completed his tenure in December 2024.

🎓 36 experts. 16 African countries. Knowledge shared. Capacity built. Mission advanced. This week in Abidjan 🇨🇮, scientists from across French-speaking Africa came together for an intensive CTBTO training course, learning to access and analyse data from our International Monitoring System (IMS) and turning it into knowledge their countries can use. Over five days, participants worked hands-on with real waveform data: detecting and locating seismic events, mastering NDC-in-a-Box and Geotool, while exploring how the same technology reaches far beyond its core mission. Among them were women scientists helping to shape the #NextGen of National Data Centres in their region - expertise that stays in their countries long after the course ends. Held with Côte d'Ivoire's Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, this regional workshop for Francophone Africa aligns with our #NDCs4All initiative to ensure every State Signatory can fully benefit from the Treaty. In the CTBT's 30th anniversary year, capacity like this is how a 🌍 verification system becomes truly global. One Treaty. One Goal. Zero Tests. 🕊️ Learn more about NDCs4All: ctbto.info/NDCs4All

Two hundred years later, the vision remains the same: dialogue over division, cooperation over isolation, and solidarity over indifference. The challenges facing our hemisphere, from democratic governance and security to development and inequality, require collective action grounded in shared principles and mutual respect. The @OAS_official is modernizing to better serve our member states and the peoples of the Americas. Together, we must carry forward the promise of those who envisioned a more united hemisphere and continue working toward peace, prosperity, democracy, and opportunity for all. Video

Today, ahead of the 56th #OASAssembly in Panama, we met with representatives of civil society, Indigenous peoples, Afro-descendant communities, workers, youth, and the private sector to discuss the challenges and opportunities facing our hemisphere. Democracy, security, human rights, development, and social inclusion cannot be advanced by governments alone. We need a whole-of-society approach that ensures communities are heard and that public policies are informed by the experiences and perspectives of the people they serve. The diversity of the Americas is one of our greatest strengths. By building trust, fostering dialogue, and working together as partners, we can transform that diversity into a foundation for greater peace, prosperity, and opportunity across the hemisphere. Video

A Olimpíada reúne anualmente mais de 18 milhões de estudantes e esta premiação acontece em um momento de fortalecimento das políticas voltadas ao ensino da matemática na educação básica. Além do apoio à Obmep, o MEC coordena o Compromisso Nacional Toda Matemática, iniciativa que busca ampliar a aprendizagem dos estudantes em todo o país. A educação é a base e o caminho para o desenvolvimento do país e da sociedade. EL DETRÁS DE ESCENA DEL ICÓNICO FESTEJO DE MESSI CON UN PERIODISTA ARGENTINO ANTE AUSTRIA: “ES EL MEJOR DÍA DE MI VIDA” El partido entre Argentina y Austria por la segunda fecha del Grupo J en el Mundial 2026 dejó una imagen que circuló por las redes sociales antes de que terminara el partido: Lionel Messi, tras convertir el segundo gol en el AT&T Stadium de Dallas, fue corriendo hacia el córner izquierdo y en el medio se cruzó con un periodista, a quien le chocó las palmas y según confesó, el astro rosarino lo dejó temblando. La escena quedó registrada por las cámaras y se propagó de inmediato. Cinco minutos después del gol, el teléfono de Bruno ya estaba lleno de mensajes: sus contactos le enviaban la foto del momento. "Me llevo este momento y una imagen para toda la vida", expresó el periodista. Ante las cámaras del canal, Bruno no ocultó el estado en que lo dejó el episodio. “No, estoy temblando”, fue lo primero que atinó a decir. Cuando le preguntaron por qué, respondió: “Vino Leo a festejar el segundo acá, me vio gritándolo y se tiró y le toqué la mano, le dije: ‘Leo, no lo puedo creer’“. Y agregó: “Estoy medio ido, pero no lo puedo creer. Es uno de los mejores días de mi vida periodística”. 📲 Lea la nota completa 🔗infob.ae/4vJp80R
